sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to the first episode of The Rest is History, our new podcast about all things historical.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《一切皆历史》（The Rest is History）第一集，这是我们一档全新的播客节目，内容包罗万象，古今皆谈。

sentences.en: I'm Dominic Sandbrook, and my sidekick, as I like to refer to him, although he would no doubt refer to himself as my puppet master, is opposite me, and it's Mr Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 我是多米尼克·桑德布鲁克（Dominic Sandbrook），坐在我对面的是我的“跟班”——我是这么叫他的，虽然他毫无疑问会自封为我的幕后操纵者——汤姆·霍兰（Tom Holland）先生。

sentences.en: Hello, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你好，汤姆。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，多米尼克。

sentences.en: What an ambivalent introduction that was.
sentences.zh: 这开场白可真够意味深长的。

sentences.en: Lovely to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: You looking forward to the podcast?
sentences.zh: 你很期待这档播客吗？

sentences.en: Done a podcast before?
sentences.zh: 以前做过播客吗？

sentences.en: I've never done a podcast before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未做过播客。

sentences.en: I've been on lots, but I've never actually done one.
sentences.zh: 我上过很多次，但自己确实没做过。

sentences.en: But since everybody else in Britain is doing one, I thought that...
sentences.zh: 但既然英国其他人都在做，我想……

sentences.en: Not one like this, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，可不是这种的。

sentences.en: Not one like this.
sentences.zh: 不是这种的。

sentences.en: No, not one like this.
sentences.zh: 对，不是这种的。

sentences.en: This is going to be something completely and radically new.
sentences.zh: 这将是一档完全且彻底焕然一新的节目。

sentences.en: Well, that remains to be seen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这还有待观察。

sentences.en: Tom Credentials?
sentences.zh: 汤姆的资历？

sentences.en: Historian of the ancient world, early Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 古代史、中世纪早期的历史学家。

sentences.en: I've just written a book, Dominion, which goes from 480 BC, right the way up to the present day, a history of Christianity called Dominion, available in all good bookshops, folks.
sentences.zh: 我刚写了一本书叫《多明利恩》（Dominion），上起公元前480年，一直写到今天，是一部关于基督教的历史，书名叫《多明利恩》，各大优质书店均有售，各位朋友。

sentences.en: It's a very good book, even if I say so myself.
sentences.zh: 这本书写得非常好，尽管这话由我来说有点自吹自擂。

sentences.en: A very good book, Tom.
sentences.zh: 确实是一本好书，汤姆。

sentences.en: And you?
sentences.zh: 那你呢？

sentences.en: And I write about modern Britain mainly, a little bit in America, but mainly modern Britain.
sentences.zh: 我主要写现代英国，也涉及一点美国，但主要是现代英国。

sentences.en: So I've written a series of books about Britain since the 1950s, and the most recent one is called Who Dares Wins, and it's all about Margaret Thatcher in the 80s and Duran Duran
sentences.zh: 所以我写了一系列关于20世纪50年代以来英国的书，最近的一本叫《谁敢赢》（Who Dares Wins），主要讲述80年代的玛格丽特·撒切尔、杜兰杜兰乐队（Duran Duran），

sentences.en: and Spandau Ballet and the Falklands War, and everything you would ever want to know.
sentences.zh: 还有斯潘道芭蕾乐队（Spandau Ballet）、马岛战争，以及你所能想了解的一切。

sentences.en: So I'm batting for the ancient Romans.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在为古罗马摇旗呐喊。

sentences.en: Dominic is batting for Duran Duran.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克则是在为杜兰杜兰乐队摇旗呐喊。

sentences.en: We're covering all the bases there, I like to think.
sentences.zh: 我想我们把各方面都兼顾到了。

sentences.en: So essentially, we can cover almost anything, and that, of course, is a great joy of podcasts.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，我们几乎可以讨论任何事情，当然，这也是播客的最大乐趣所在。

sentences.en: And Dominic, what do you want to talk about today?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，今天你想聊点什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think we should start as we mean to go on, and I think we should start with greatness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们应该一开场就定下基调，我觉得我们应该从“伟大”开始聊起。

sentences.en: Who is great?
sentences.zh: 谁是伟大的？

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 什么是伟大？

sentences.en: And why aren't people great anymore?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在的人都不伟大了？

sentences.en: So, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: As a great man yourself, throw some great figures from history at me.
sentences.zh: 作为你自己就是一个伟大的人，快给我抛出几个历史上的伟大人物吧。

sentences.en: Well, the biggie, of course, is Alexander, the great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，头号大咖，当然是亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: Well, you see, I think what's interesting is that the idea of somebody being great isn't actually a kind of natural thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，我觉得有趣的是，“某人是伟大的”这种想法实际上并不是一种自然产物。

sentences.en: It's something that's bred of very specific cultural circumstances.
sentences.zh: 它是孕育于非常特殊的文化环境之中的产物。

sentences.en: And the idea that somebody can be great is originally a Persian idea.
sentences.zh: 而且“某人可以成为伟大之人”这种观念，最初是一个波斯概念。

sentences.en: The great king, is it?
sentences.zh: 万王之王，是吧？

sentences.en: The great king.
sentences.zh: 万王之王。

sentences.en: So he's the king of the kings.
sentences.zh: 所以他是诸王之王。

sentences.en: He's the great king.
sentences.zh: 他是伟大的国王。

sentences.en: That's how he's known.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么出名的。

sentences.en: So the king of Persia was superior to...
sentences.zh: 所以波斯国王凌驾于……

sentences.en: Because the Persian Empire is the greatest empire that anyone had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 因为波斯帝国是人们所见过的最伟大的帝国。

sentences.en: And I just increasingly think that basically everything goes back to Persia, ultimately.
sentences.zh: 而且我越来越觉得，基本上所有事情归根结底都源于波斯。

sentences.en: Everything kind of, you know, you follow something...
sentences.zh: 事情基本上就是，你知道，你顺着某条线索去追溯……

sentences.en: That'll go down very well with people in Iran.
sentences.zh: 这话在伊朗人听来可不太对劲。

sentences.en: Well, you follow things extremely.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你把事情推演到极致。

sentences.en: It always goes back to Persia.
sentences.zh: 总能追溯到波斯。

sentences.en: And so the king of Persia is the great king.
sentences.zh: 因此，波斯国王就是伟大的国王。

sentences.en: And then Alexander III of Macedon conquers the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 然后马其顿的亚历山大三世征服了波斯帝国。

sentences.en: So he then becomes the great king.
sentences.zh: 于是他接着成为了伟大的国王。

sentences.en: So this is what, 4th century BC?
sentences.zh: 所以这是什么时候？公元前4世纪？

sentences.en: Yeah, 4th century.
sentences.zh: 对，公元前4世纪。

sentences.en: So he dies and his empire splits up.
sentences.zh: 然后他死了，他的帝国四分五裂。

sentences.en: And his various generals kind of scavenge over it like a pack of hyenas.
sentences.zh: 他的各路将领像一群鬣狗一样在上面争抢分食。

sentences.en: And they all want to be like Alexander.
sentences.zh: 他们都想成为亚历山大那样的人。

sentences.en: And there's one king in particular called Antiochus who goes back into Persia, tries to reconquer it.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个叫安条克的国王，曾打回波斯，试图重新征服它。

sentences.en: And he adopts the name of great, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎他也采用了“伟大”这个称号。

sentences.en: So he's calling himself the great king.
sentences.zh: 所以他自称为伟大的国王。

sentences.en: So there's a hint there that this is where it begins.
sentences.zh: 这就暗示了这或许就是这一传统的起源。

sentences.en: But then what actually happens is that it's the Romans who pick up on it.
sentences.zh: 但随后真正发生的是，罗马人继承了这一传统。

sentences.en: So the first reference to Alexander is in the mid-3rd century.
sentences.zh: 因此，对亚历山大的首次提及是在公元前3世纪中期。

sentences.en: AD or BC?
sentences.zh: 公元后还是公元前？

sentences.en: Sorry, BC.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是公元前。

sentences.en: And they are calling him Alexander Magnus, Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 他们称他为“马格努斯亚历山大”，也就是亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: So basically, Dominic, what I'm saying is that the idea of greatness comes from ancient history.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，多米尼克，我的意思是，“伟大”这个概念源于古代历史。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以这太妙了。

sentences.en: So basically that's mine.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这就是我的观点。

sentences.en: But you, of course, you're a modern historian.
sentences.zh: 但你，当然了，你是一位现代历史学家。

sentences.en: So, I mean, basically you don't have great people.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，基本上你们没有那种伟大人物。

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 对，没有真正的伟大人物。

sentences.en: So I obviously, I do my research for this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，为了这期播客我做了研究。

sentences.en: So I looked at the Wikipedia list of people.
sentences.zh: 我查阅了维基百科上的伟人名单。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 厉害。

sentences.en: I found another website, which I'm rustling my paper to prove that I've done my research.
sentences.zh: 我又找到了另一个网站——我正在哗啦哗啦翻动纸张以证明我确实做过研究。

sentences.en: Another website which begins with the words, history has produced at least 38 great people.
sentences.zh: 另一个网站开篇第一句是：历史至少产生过38位伟大人物。

sentences.en: At least 38.
sentences.zh: 至少38位。

sentences.en: It's very precise.
sentences.zh: 这个数字很精确嘛。

sentences.en: There could be some more out there.
sentences.zh: 外面可能还有更多。

sentences.en: It could be 43.
sentences.zh: 也许有43位。

sentences.en: Waiting to be captured.
sentences.zh: 正等待着被发掘。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: But anyway, let's go back to the Wikipedia, because Wikipedia is obviously the one thing that people will look at.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，让我们回到维基百科，因为维基百科显然是人们最常查阅的网站。

sentences.en: So what's the most recent?
sentences.zh: 那么最近的是谁？

sentences.en: So I think the most recent is the Emperor Meiji of Japan.
sentences.zh: 我想最近的一位是日本的明治天皇。

sentences.en: He dies in 1912.
sentences.zh: 他在1912年去世。

sentences.en: So he's the guy who opens up Japan to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他就是那个向西方打开日本国门的人。

sentences.en: He modernizes Japan and sort of pushes it into the 20th century, if you like.
sentences.zh: 他使日本实现现代化，并可以说是将日本推入了20世纪。

sentences.en: But everybody before that.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前的所有人。

sentences.en: So the last people that we think of as great are kind of Peter the Great.
sentences.zh: 我们认为算得上伟大的人，最后大概就是彼得大帝。

sentences.en: Catherine the Great.
sentences.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜大帝。

sentences.en: Catherine the Great.
sentences.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜大帝。

sentences.en: So we're talking beginning of the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论的是18世纪初。

sentences.en: Then we've got the enlightened despots.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有了开明专制君主。

sentences.en: I mean, I found them excruciatingly boring, actually, when I did them for a level.
sentences.zh: 说实话，当年我为了高级水平考试（A-level）学习他们的时候，觉得他们无聊透顶。

sentences.en: Catherine the Great, Frederick the Great.
sentences.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜大帝、腓特烈大帝。

sentences.en: People who modernize Russia and Prussia and these sort of central European monarchies.
sentences.zh: 那些使俄国、普鲁士以及这类中欧君主国实现现代化的统治者。

sentences.en: But who is deciding that they're great?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是谁在决定他们是否伟大？

sentences.en: I mean, is there a kind of selection committee, like the Nobel Prize?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是不是有一个类似诺贝尔奖那样的评选委员会？

sentences.en: No, I think it emerges from the sort of immediate historiography.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这是从当时的史学研究中自然涌现出来的。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of creation of Victorian writers.
sentences.zh: 所以这可以说是维多利亚时代作家的创造。

sentences.en: And I think greatness in this, when we talk about people being great, I think a lot of it is to do with sort of nation building, state builders.
sentences.zh: 我认为当我们谈论某人伟大时，其中很大一部分与民族国家构建者、国家缔造者有关。

sentences.en: And I think it's the thing that Victorians did.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这是维多利亚时代的人所做的事。

sentences.en: I mean, as you know, the Victorians or 19th century nationalists generally were all about finding historical roots of nation states and arguing that,
sentences.zh: 如你所知，维多利亚时代的人或19th世纪的民族主义者普遍热衷于寻找民族国家的历史根源，并论证说，

sentences.en: you know, they would sort of delve back into the archives to prove that a given nation had sort of been born unsullied and pure at the dawn of history.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会深入故纸堆中翻找档案，以证明某个特定的民族在历史的曙光初现时就已清白纯洁地诞生了。

sentences.en: And I think they looked for founding fathers.
sentences.zh: 我想他们在寻找国父。

sentences.en: And they were generally, I mean, they were Catherine the Great, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 他们通常都是——我想叶卡捷琳娜大帝算一个。

sentences.en: But by and large, they're men, they're warriors who've welded their people into this sort of mighty realm or modernized it or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，他们都是男性，都是把他们的人民凝聚成如此强大帝国或使其实现现代化的勇士之类的人物。

sentences.en: But it's, so in which case, why is George Washington not George the Great?
sentences.zh: 但是，既然如此，为什么乔治·华盛顿不是“伟大的乔治”呢？

sentences.en: Because he's a founder, I mean, he's the essence of a founding father.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一位缔造者，我的意思是，他就是国父的本质。

sentences.en: Well, this is the thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题就在这里，不是吗？

sentences.en: Is it because it's a republic?
sentences.zh: 是因为这是一个共和国吗？

sentences.en: Well, you could go with the, I mean.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以这么认为，我的意思是。

sentences.en: So you can't have great men in republics?
sentences.zh: 所以你在共和国里就不能有伟人？

sentences.en: No, you do have great men.
sentences.zh: 不，你确实有伟人。

sentences.en: And to just concentrate on America for a second, they don't use that terminology, but they do use the terminology of the founding fathers.
sentences.zh: 如果只把目光集中在美国一秒钟，他们虽然不用“伟大”这个术语，但他们确实使用了“国父”这个术语。

sentences.en: And they have, you know, the Lincoln Memorial, the Jefferson Monument.
sentences.zh: 而且他们拥有，你知道的，林肯纪念堂、杰斐逊纪念堂。

sentences.en: They have all these kind of, you know, you can go to kind of Monticello,
sentences.zh: 他们拥有所有这些，你知道的，你可以去参观诸如蒙蒂塞洛之类的建筑，

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson's house and kind of do homage to the great man.
sentences.zh: 也就是托马斯·杰斐逊的故居，去向这位伟人顶礼膜拜。

sentences.en: But I think the fact that they're not, it's not Abraham the Great.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他们不叫“伟大的亚伯拉罕”，这本身就说明了问题。

sentences.en: It's not George the Great.
sentences.zh: 他们不叫“伟大的乔治”。

sentences.en: But I think that that does suggest that there is an issue with, in republics.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这确实表明在共和国里存在着一个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许吧。

sentences.en: And indeed democracies with the idea of, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且在民主政体中，对于这种观念确实也存在问题。

sentences.en: Well, I definitely think that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我绝对这么认为。

sentences.en: Of calling someone great.
sentences.zh: 也就是称呼某人为“伟大”这件事情。

sentences.en: I absolutely think you're right about that.
sentences.zh: 对于这一点，我绝对认为你是对的。

sentences.en: So these are all monarchs.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人全都是君主。

sentences.en: So I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想。

sentences.en: Is there anyone who's called, who is, who's called great, who's not a monarch?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么人被称为“伟大”，但他不是君主的？

sentences.en: I mean, Pompey the Great, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，庞培大帝（Pompey the Great），我猜算一个。

sentences.en: There are some earls and bishops.
sentences.zh: 还有一些伯爵和主教。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm going back to the Wikipedia list, but it's a bit desperate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我是根据维基百科的名单来说的，但这多少有点勉强。

sentences.en: But basically they're all monarchs.
sentences.zh: 但基本上他们全都是君主。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think almost by, isn't it true that by definition in a democracy, you can't have a, the great.
sentences.zh: 我认为几乎可以这样说：难道在民主政体中，根据定义就不可能存在“大人物”吗？

sentences.en: Because an awful lot of people, often actually a majority, may well have voted for other candidates.
sentences.zh: 因为相当多的人，甚至往往是大多数人，很可能把票投给了其他候选人。

sentences.en: May well have voted against them.
sentences.zh: 很可能曾投票反对过他们。

sentences.en: But also it's an, isn't it that it's an offense against the very idea of, of, of democratic.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是一种，难道这不也是对民主理念本身的冒犯吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the, the, the, the kind of implicit egalitarianism of a republic or a democracy, the idea that there are great people,
sentences.zh: 你知道，共和国或民主政体中那种内含的平等主义，即认为存在着伟大之人的这种观念，

sentences.en: great men who put democracies in their shadow is seen as being threatened.
sentences.zh: 那些将民主政体置于其阴影之下的伟人，被视为构成了威胁。

sentences.en: A lot of democracies do have that there, don't they?
sentences.zh: 很多民主国家确实有那种称号，对吧？

sentences.en: So his.
sentences.zh: 他的也是。

sentences.en: Yeah, but they don't call them great.
sentences.zh: 对，但他们不叫他们“伟大”。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你不会。

sentences.en: What about Mustafa Kemal, Ataturk, Father Turk, the founder of modern Turkey.
sentences.zh: 那穆斯塔法·凯末尔、阿塔图尔克、土耳其之父、现代土耳其的缔造者呢？

sentences.en: So there's a man, I mean, effectively, I mean, they, he, he is, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一个人，我的意思是，实际上，我是说，他们，他，他，你知道的。

sentences.en: But he's, he invents, but he's another kind of founding father who's sticking it all together.
sentences.zh: 但他，他创造了，但他又是另一种把一切粘合在一起的开国元勋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，对。

sentences.en: So he's, so there are some 20th century examples.

sentences.en: And I think that there is a feeling that Churchill, on that measurement of greatness, doesn't quite measure up because he's seen, you know, he has racist views.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们有一种感觉，即丘吉尔用这种伟大的标准去衡量的话，似乎还不够格，因为他被认为，你知道的，持有种族主义观点。

sentences.en: You mentioned the arc of history.
sentences.zh: 你提到了历史的弧线。

sentences.en: He's seen as somebody who's on the wrong side of a lot of...
sentences.zh: 他被视为什么许多……站在历史错误一面的人。

sentences.en: Yes, well, I mean, he was...
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，我的意思是，他曾经……

sentences.en: I mean, even by the standards of the time, he was a huge reactionary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使以当时的标准来看，他也是个极端的保守派。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But in a way, the fact that people are sort of daubing racist on his statue is proof of greatness because if he weren't great, I mean, who would care?
sentences.zh: 但从某种程度上说，人们在他的雕像上涂抹“种族主义者”这一事实，恰恰证明了他的伟大，因为如果他不伟大，我的意思是，谁会在乎呢？

sentences.en: You know, if he was some sort of middle-ranking prime minister.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果他只是个什么中等水平的首相。

sentences.en: Well, I think that that's a kind of...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一种……

sentences.en: It's an attack not just on Churchill but on an understanding of greatness that is now very, very contested.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是对丘吉尔的攻击，也是对一种现在备受争议的“伟大”理解的攻击。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that it kind of...
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这有点……

sentences.en: Also, it kind of blurs in with the fact that the main island in the UK is called Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 此外，这也与英国的主岛被称为“大不列颠”（Great Britain）这一事实混淆在了一起。

sentences.en: Obviously, it has nothing to do with the fact that Britain objectively is great.
sentences.zh: 显然，这与英国客观上很伟大没有任何关系。

sentences.en: It's simply the fact that the island of Britain is bigger than Little Britain, which is Brittany.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是因为不列颠岛比小不列颠（即布列塔尼）要大。

sentences.en: So that's why it's Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以它才叫大不列颠。

sentences.en: It's an expression of geographical size.
sentences.zh: 这只是地理尺度的一种表达。

sentences.en: But I think that, obviously, over Britain's imperial heyday, there was a tendency to say, yeah, we're great.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，显然，在英国帝国的全盛时期，人们倾向于说，对，我们很伟大。

sentences.en: Sort of nominative determinism, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 有点像名义决定论，对吧？

sentences.en: Nominative determinism, yes.
sentences.zh: 名义决定论，是的。

sentences.en: And I think that Churchill is the kind of archetypal poster boy for that idea of Britain being great.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为丘吉尔可以说是这种“英国很伟大”理念的典型代言人。

sentences.en: And so I think that also is something that is being attacked because part of, I suppose, of what's in the back of the minds
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这也是遭到抨击的原因之一，因为我想，在那些将丘吉尔视为英国问题象征的人的心中，

sentences.en: of people who see Churchill as a problematic emblem for Britain is the sense that his model of greatness is something that is essentially to be rejected, that it's militarist,
sentences.zh: 潜藏着这样一种感觉：他的伟大模式本质上是应该被拒绝的，它是军国主义的，

sentences.en: that it's supremacist, that it's...
sentences.zh: 它是至上主义的，它是……

sentences.en: But all great, all the people we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 但所有伟大的……我们谈论过的所有人。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，嗯，对。

sentences.en: ...fit into that, with the exception of Nelson Mandela and Gandhi.
sentences.zh: ……都符合这一点，纳尔逊·曼德拉和甘地除外。

sentences.en: But that, again, feeds into the idea that we're talking about a model of greatness, an idea of greatness that feels old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 但这也再次印证了我们的观点，即我们正在讨论的一种伟大的模式、一种让人感觉过时的伟大观念。

sentences.en: Does it feel old-fashioned, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，真的觉得过时吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得是的。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得。

sentences.en: If you're Chinese, Xi Jinping, will he not be great one day?
sentences.zh: 如果你是中国人，习近平，他难道有一天不会成为伟人吗？

sentences.en: Or Vladimir Putin?
sentences.zh: 或者弗拉基米尔·普京？

sentences.en: But again, this is the communist thing, that he can't be enshrined as a great man, say, in the way that the emperor was or the first emperor.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，这就是共产主义的问题所在，他不能像过去的皇帝或始皇帝那样，被奉为伟人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, China obviously has always had a kind of sense of the great man because it's born with it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，中国显然一直有一种“伟人”的意识，因为这是与生俱来的。

sentences.en: The first emperor is seen as, you know, very much in the style that we've been talking about as the guy who creates a state, who fashions an empire, who fashions an order.
sentences.zh: 始皇帝被视为我们一直在谈论的那种典型风格——一个创建国家、塑造帝国、建立秩序的人。

sentences.en: And that inheritance runs right the way down to the abolition of the figure of the emperor in the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这种传承一直延续到20世纪初皇帝制度的废除。

sentences.en: But, and obviously Mao and all, you know, Deng Xiaoping and now, that there is a sense in which the figure of the emperor is someone who's absent.
sentences.zh: 但是，显然还有毛泽东、邓小平以及现在的人，在某种意义上，皇帝这个角色是缺席的。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of like losing a limb or something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这有点像失去了一肢或者什么的。

sentences.en: But China is officially a communist state.
sentences.zh: 但中国官方是一个共产主义国家。

sentences.en: And so I think ideologically there isn't a place for greatness in that kind of Thomas Carlyle sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在意识形态上，在托马斯·卡莱尔那种意义上，并没有容纳伟大的空间。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很准确。

sentences.en: I think there is a place.
sentences.zh: 我认为是有空间的。

sentences.en: I mean, the great helmsman, Mao, all those people, you know, waving their little red books.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，伟大的舵手毛泽东，所有那些人，你知道的，挥舞着他们的小红书。

sentences.en: Yes, but there is a tension there.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这里面存在一种张力。

sentences.en: They can't, the Chinese cannot celebrate Mao as great in the way that the fascists celebrate Hitler as great.
sentences.zh: 他们不能，中国人不能像法西斯分子崇拜希特勒那样去崇拜毛泽东的伟大。

sentences.en: It's odd, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or even, I mean, I don't think that you would get a Chinese general secretary, for instance, behaving in the way that Trump behaved when he returned from his COVID.
sentences.zh: 甚至，我的意思是，我觉得你不会看到某位中国总书记的表现像特朗普从新冠中康复归来时那样。

sentences.en: Take his mask off and saluting.
sentences.zh: 摘下口罩，敬礼。

sentences.en: I think all of those, you know, that was, whatever you think of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些，你知道的，不管你怎么看。

sentences.en: Vladimir Putin would behave.
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京就会这么做。

sentences.en: Putin would take his top off.
sentences.zh: 普京会脱掉上衣。

sentences.en: Putin absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 普京绝对会。

sentences.en: And actually the fact that Churchill, that Churchill, Jesus Christ, what a terrible slip.
sentences.zh: 事实上，丘吉尔，丘吉尔——天哪，真是口误。

sentences.en: Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普。

sentences.en: Freudian slip there.
sentences.zh: 那是弗洛伊德式的口误。

sentences.en: Oh, I'll never let that go.
sentences.zh: 哦，我永远不会放过这个梗。

sentences.en: The fact that Trump does behave in that way, and obviously his make America great again stuff,
sentences.zh: 事实上，特朗普确实会有那样的举动，显然还有他那些“让美国再次伟大”的口号，

sentences.en: actually shows you just how deeply the concept of greatness is embedded in the American sort of political psyche.
sentences.zh: 其实向你展示了“伟大”这个概念在美式政治心理中根深蒂固到了什么程度。

sentences.en: The whole iconography of the presidency actually is all the great man kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 总统职位的整套意象其实全都是那一套伟人作派。

sentences.en: And that kind of feeds back to what we were talking about, you know, about the relationship between Rome and America.
sentences.zh: 这就呼应了我们刚才谈到的，关于罗马和美国之间关系的话题。

sentences.en: I think that there is a huge part of what makes many, many Americans very, very uncomfortable about Trump is the sense that he is pushing that model of greatness too far.
sentences.zh: 我认为，让许多美国人对特朗普感到非常非常不适的一个重要原因，就在于他们觉得他把那种伟大的模式推得太远了。

sentences.en: It's all, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 全都是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, when I was doing my PhD in history, the idea that I'd be doing a podcast about greatness would have been anathema,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我攻读历史学博士学位时，如果有人告诉我我会去做一个关于“伟大”的播客，那简直是天方夜谭，

sentences.en: because the very idea of greatness to sort of academic historians is complete nonsense and, you know, unthinkable and not worth giving house room to.
sentences.zh: 因为在学院派历史学家看来，“伟大”这个概念纯粹是无稽之谈，是不可想象的，根本不值一提。

sentences.en: And we would, you know, have these sort of seminars where somebody would say X is great, everyone would kind of scoff.
sentences.zh: 我们以前会开那种研讨会，当有人说某某很伟大时，大家都会发出嘲笑。

sentences.en: But then we'd go to the pub and have this big debate about who was greater, Pele or Maradona or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但随后我们就会去酒吧，激烈争论究竟是谁更伟大，是贝利、马拉多纳还是别的什么人。

sentences.en: So the idea of greatness.
sentences.zh: 所以关于“伟大”这个概念……

sentences.en: Well, sport, yes, because in sport you can measure it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，体育是可以的，因为在体育里你可以衡量它。

sentences.en: Well, you can't measure it, though, can you?
sentences.zh: 不过，其实你也无法衡量，对吧？

sentences.en: You can't measure.
sentences.zh: 你无法衡量。

sentences.en: You kind of can.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上其实可以。

sentences.en: Muhammad Ali, of course, famously said, I am the greateSt.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里，当然了，曾有一句名言：我是最伟大的。

sentences.en: He basically created his own myth, which all great men and women do to some extent, didn't it?
sentences.zh: 他基本上创造了自己的神话，所有伟大的男人和女人某种程度上不都这样吗？

sentences.en: And Maradona, the same.
sentences.zh: 马拉多纳也是一样。

sentences.en: But part of the appeal of sport is that it provides a stage on which these, you know, the desire for hero worship can be channeled safely.
sentences.zh: 但体育的魅力部分在于，它提供了一个舞台，让人们对英雄崇拜的渴望能够安全地宣泄出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But that's, I mean, history is no different, surely.
sentences.zh: 但那——我的意思是，历史也没什么不同，肯定的。

sentences.en: No, because I think that history suggests that, you know, giving a stage to people who see themselves as great and who are seen by other people as great can threaten disaster.
sentences.zh: 不，因为我认为历史表明，你知道的，给那些自认为是伟人、也被其他人视为伟人的人提供舞台，可能会招致灾难。

sentences.en: If you live in a democracy or a republic.
sentences.zh: 如果你生活在民主国家或共和国里的话。

sentences.en: See, I think if we went into Waterstones now, to the children's section, to the history section, I mean, they have the horrible histories, but it is all, you know, inspiring girls,
sentences.zh: 你看，我想如果我们现在走进水石书店，去儿童区、历史区，我的意思是，那里有《糟糕的历史》系列，但全都是，你知道的，鼓舞人心的女孩，

sentences.en: wonderful girls or whatever.
sentences.zh: 杰出的女性之类的。

sentences.en: Those kind of books, you know, the ones I mean.
sentences.zh: 那种书，你知道我指的是哪种。

sentences.en: And it's Amelia Earhart, Marie Curie, Agatha Christie, Rosa Parks.
sentences.zh: 里面有埃米莉亚·埃尔哈特、玛丽·居里、阿加莎·克里斯蒂、罗莎·帕克斯。

sentences.en: I mean, Rosa Parks is somebody who's clearly conceived by lots of people as great, as a great figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，罗莎·帕克斯显然被许多人视为一个伟大的人，一个伟大的传奇人物。

sentences.en: I don't think the word great is adequate, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我觉得“伟大”这个词并不贴切。

sentences.en: I think, I don't think that's, I don't think the model of greatness, as it's traditionally understood.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，我不认为那是……我不认为传统意义上理解的“伟大”模式适合她。

sentences.en: She has the moral qualities that allowed her to be on the right side of history, to transcend her time, to lead her people, to be the vessel for something bigger than herself.
sentences.zh: 她具备了种种道德品质，使她能够站在历史正确的一边，超越自己的时代，引领她的人民，成为承载某种超越自身之物的载体。

sentences.en: But again, this goes back to the sense in which, you know, if we are going to talk about people like that as being great, it's because we're talking about moral greatness.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，这就回到了我们刚才说的意思，如果我们打算把这样的人称为伟大，那是因为我们在谈论的是道德上的伟大。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But can you, I mean, you're basically saying there was martial greatness and then moral greatness, but I think the two have always been.
sentences.zh: 但你能……我的意思是，你基本上是在说曾经有武功的伟大，然后是道德的伟大，但我认为这两者向来都是……

sentences.en: I think, I think it's because we're, we're uncomfortable with, with the word saint, but I think that, that actually, that actually someone like, like,
sentences.zh: 我想，我想这是因为我们，我们对“圣人”这个词感到不自在，但我觉得，实际上，实际上像，像，

sentences.en: like Mandela or Martin Luther King.
sentences.zh: 像曼德拉或马丁·路德·金这样的人……

sentences.en: Oh, because we would have otherwise have called them a saint.
sentences.zh: 哦，因为否则我们就会称他们为圣人了。

sentences.en: That, that, yeah, that, that the emotions that they inspire are the emotions that traditionally saints have inspired.
sentences.zh: 对，那种，那种……他们激发的情感，正是传统上圣人所激发的情感。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's very true.
sentences.zh: 对，这非常真实。

sentences.en: So they're kind of secular saints.
sentences.zh: 所以他们某种程度上是世俗圣人。

sentences.en: I buy that.
sentences.zh: 我赞同这一点。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: And I think that that's like, I think, I think it's different.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这就像是……我觉得，我觉得这不一样。

sentences.en: People visit their, their, their, their shrines, they get relics.
sentences.zh: 人们去参拜他们的圣地，收集他们的遗物。

sentences.en: But also they're seen as, as, as, as morally inspirational and that if you behave like them, then you will make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们也被视为在道德上具有鼓舞作用，如果你效仿他们的行为，你就会让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: I think that that's a key part of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是其中的一个关键部分。

sentences.en: Whereas if you behave like Frederick the Great, you're going to end up in a bunker in, in Berlin.
sentences.zh: 而如果你效仿腓特烈大帝的行为，你最后只会落得个困死在柏林地堡里的下场。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Attacked by the Soviets.
sentences.zh: 遭到苏联人的攻击。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think that's not the fate I want for myself.
sentences.zh: 我想这不是我为自己选择的命运。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: Um, so I think, I think that, um, I think it's kind of the, the ambivalent attitude to, to, to, to, well, obviously I think everything comes down to Christianity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我想，我觉得，嗯，我觉得这有点像是对……对……对……显然我觉得一切都可以归结为基督教。

sentences.en: But I think in, in, in, in the West it's, it's, we're uncomfortable, you know, we remain sufficiently Christian that we're uncomfortable with the idea of great men.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在西方，我们感到不自在，你知道的，我们依然保留了足够的基督教传统，以至于我们对“伟人”的概念感到不自在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because we recognize that there is an aspect of that greatness that is kind of pagan almost, that it's, it's a kind of classical ideal that, that, that,
sentences.zh: 因为我们意识到，那种伟大中有一个方面几乎是异教徒式的，它是一种古典理想，而这种理想……

sentences.en: that morally we're uncomfortable with.
sentences.zh: 我们在道德上对此感到不适。

sentences.en: But we're insufficiently Christian that we're happy now to talk about saints.
sentences.zh: 但我们的基督教色彩又不够浓厚，以至于我们现在很乐意去谈论圣人。

sentences.en: All right then, Tom, you need to pick three people now who you think are great and they've got to be alive right now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，你现在得选出三个人，你认为他们是伟人，而且他们现在还活着。

sentences.en: Maybe they can be out of office.
sentences.zh: 也许他们已经不在任上了。

sentences.en: But why, why have I got to, because I don't, you're posing this wrong.
sentences.zh: 但为什么，为什么我必须……因为我不想，你这个问题设定的方向就不对。

sentences.en: Just on my own way to look foolish.
sentences.zh: 这只会让我自取其辱。

sentences.en: I, you see, I, I, I don't think that this is an age where people are great.
sentences.zh: 我，你看，我，我，我认为现在这个时代根本不出伟人。

sentences.en: I'll tell you who will disagree with you, Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你谁会不同意你的看法——鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: He believes in greatness.
sentences.zh: 他相信伟大。

sentences.en: Do you think one day people will call him Boris the Great or Boris the Fat?
sentences.zh: 你觉得有一天人们会叫他“伟大的鲍里斯”还是“肥胖的鲍里斯”？

sentences.en: Boris the Fat.
sentences.zh: 肥胖的鲍里斯。

sentences.en: Boris, Boris, Boris, not as fat as he was.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯，鲍里斯，鲍里斯，没以前那么胖了。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, so Boris, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，所以，所以鲍里斯，绝对的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a, yeah, Trump, obviously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一个，对，特朗普，显然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得……

sentences.en: Donald the Great.
sentences.zh: 伟大的唐纳德。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, I think that there's a kind of.
sentences.zh: 对，我想，我想这有点像……

sentences.en: With that accent.
sentences.zh: 带着那种口音。

sentences.en: Maybe, maybe a definition of, of a populist leader is that he would like to think of himself as being called the Great.
sentences.zh: 也许，民粹主义领袖的一个定义，就是他会希望别人称自己为“大帝”或“伟大的人”。

sentences.en: Yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So that might be the definition.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许就是定义。

sentences.en: Nigel the Great.
sentences.zh: 伟大的奈杰尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, so, so, so, so by that measure, I don't think any of them.
sentences.zh: 对，所以，所以，所以，照这个标准，我觉得他们谁都不是。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you someone who I think may be remembered as the Great and called the Great would be Putin, who we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你一个我觉得可能会被后人铭记为“大帝”并被称为伟大的人，那就是我们谈论过的普京。

sentences.zh: 原因就在于，我认为普京正在创造他自己的现实。

sentences.en: Putin is creating a kind of model of Russian history in which great men do step forward and follow in the footsteps of the great leaders who came before.

sentences.en: So not Stalin, but Catherine the Great and Peter the Great, and Peter the Great particularly.

sentences.en: And so I think, you know, Catherine the Great reconquers the Crimea.

sentences.en: Yeah, I completely buy that.
sentences.zh: 对，我完全赞同这一点。

sentences.en: I think, you know, I'm not a Vladimir Putin fan.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我不是弗拉基米尔·普京的粉丝。

sentences.en: But clearly, let's say he does another 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但显然，假设他再干十年。

sentences.en: Then he goes and people will say he's transformed his country.
sentences.zh: 然后他卸任了，人们会说他改造了他的国家。

sentences.en: He's made it strong and respected on the world stage, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 他让国家变得强大并在世界舞台上受到尊敬，等等等等。

sentences.en: And Russians will, well, will sort of bow down before his image for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 而且俄罗斯人会在未来几十年里，嗯，在他的形象前顶礼膜拜。

sentences.en: Well, I think, I think, I think that it will be, he'll be called the Great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，我想，我想他会被称为大帝。

sentences.en: You know, if anyone's going to be called the Great, I think he'll be called the Great in Russia.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果有人要被称为大帝，我认为他在俄罗斯会被称为大帝。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't imagine that he'll be called it in, not in Poland or Germany.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我并不认为他会被这样称呼，在波兰或德国绝对不会。

sentences.en: Anyway, well, you said, you said three.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，嗯，你说了，你说了三个。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有三个吗？

sentences.en: Well, that was a, that was a bluff, you see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是个，那是个虚张声势，你看。

sentences.zh: 好吧，你刚才在谈论圣徒。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们会成为，他们会成为圣徒，对吧？

sentences.zh: 嗯，而且这也太饱受争议了，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我们现在的政治文化太爱争论了，以至于没人能在任何单一人物上达成一致。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 所以每个法国人，伟大的法国领袖都有这种特质。

sentences.zh: 所以戴高乐，你会说，是伟大的。

sentences.zh: 戴高乐式的法国理想是伟大的，戴高乐是伟大的。

sentences.zh: 而马克龙显然是这一传统的一部分。

sentences.zh: 这又是历史的弧线，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Saint Angela.

sentences.en: So she has a claim on that meaning of the word great, but not, in any sense, a claim on the kind of Frederick the Great model of greatness, because that's the whole point of her.
sentences.zh: 所以她对“伟大”这个词的那个含义有资格认领，但在任何意义上都没有资格认领腓特烈大帝那种模式的伟大，因为这正是她的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: She will never understand.
sentences.zh: 她永远不会理解。
